highlights.title: AI cancer cures slowed by chip shortage, says UK's biggest tech boss
highlights.summary: The head of chip designer Arm says modelling how a DNA marker is impacted by cancer cannot be done now, but computers are "going to solve it".
body: The boss of the biggest UK-headquartered tech firm has said that artifical intelligence will find a cure for cancer that humans cannot in our lifetimes.

Rene Haas, chief executive of Cambridge-based chip designer Arm Holdings, said while modelling how a DNA marker is impacted by cancer was currently "too complex" a problem, computers are "going to solve it" in the future.

Haas also told the BBC that AI would lead to widespread humanoid robots in the next five years, but that its current rapid growth was being held up by a shortage of chips needed to build data centres.
However, he was sceptical about the idea chips could be manufactured in the UK in the future.

highlights.title: Opaque recurrence, and other AI terms that you should probably know
highlights.summary: The rise of AI has brought an avalanche of new terms and slang. Here is a glossary with definitions of some of the most important words and phrases you might encounter.
body: AI is rewriting the world and, at the same time, inventing a whole new language to describe how it’s doing it. Sit in on any product meeting, pitch, or panel these days, and you’ll hear people toss around LLMs, RAG, RLHF — and, as of last week, terms like “opaque recurrence,” the reasoning technique in OpenAI’s new Astra model that’s got AI safety researchers rattled. The vocabulary moves fast enough to make even very smart people in the tech world feel a little insecure.

This glossary is our attempt to fix that: plain-English definitions of the AI terms you’re most likely to see, whether you’re building with this stuff, investing in it, or just trying to keep up by reading TechCrunch or listening to related podcasts. We update it regularly as the field evolves, so consider it a living document, much like the AI systems it describes.

highlights.title: Rybakina too strong for Osaka as Zheng stuns Swiatek at US Open
highlights.summary: Elena Rybakina cruised into the US Open quarter-finals with a straight-sets victory over Naomi Osaka to keep her push for the world No 1 ranking on track.
body: Rybakina will reclaim the top spot if she reaches the semi-finals, and after dismantling two-time champion Osaka on Louis Armstrong, she has every reason to believe she can go all the way and lift the US Open trophy.
It took the second seed just over 20 minutes to wrap up the first set 6-1 before securing a decisive break midway through the second to quell a resurgent Osaka and seal an emphatic 6-1 6-4 victory.

"I played really well today. I was feeling the ball was really good from my side," the former Wimbledon champion said. "I was a bit lucky in some moments, found some lines, but super happy with the performance.
"Naomi is a tough opponent. I knew no matter the score I needed to focus on each ball as everything can change quickly. She is also a great player. I am glad how I played today.

So, without further ado, here are the 10 most anticipated fall anime releases that are perfect for slowing down before winter.

An enhanced, remastered, and recut version of early arcs from Dragon Ball Super, Beerus reiterates the beauty of the original series’ fight choreography and the sheer scale of the events that unfold. There’s an argument to be made in favor of entire franchise arcs that are yet to be animated — after all, wouldn’t it make more sense to work on what’s left untouched, instead of enhancing a tale that already boasts several iterations?

Savvy Games Group: Brian Ward is stepping down as CEO of the Saudi-backed games conglomerate, with Turqi Alnowaiser, deputy governor of Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, taking over as interim CEO. Ward had led Savvy since 2021, overseeing a roughly $38bn investment push into the games industry that included the acquisition of Scopely and stakes in companies including Nintendo and Embracer Group.

body: Logic clearly dictates that the needs of the penne outweigh the needs of the stew, or the bun. While this would have been a gloriously fan-faithful reason for Le Creuset, the French-Belgian maker of colorful cookware for more than a century, to materialize its new limited-edition Star Trek collection, the range is being launched in celebration of 60 years of the cult sci-fi show.

No matter, because when you have such stellar items as Vulcan oven mitts, shuttlecraft baking dishes, and—perhaps best of all—a cheese grater in the shape of the classic Trek communicator (which has somewhat wonderfully been nicknamed the “Communi-grator” by Le Creuset's design team), there's only cause for celebration in the cosmos.

Going on sale today, to coincide with the space series' 60th anniversary, the limited-edition collection has actually been in development for years after Le Creuset approached Paramount to collaborate on the kitchen kit in time for the landmark birthday. Le Creuset is no stranger to fun mashups, with its recent 2024 Pokemon collection being snapped up almost instantly (those looking to get pieces now have to scour the likes of eBay for items way over original retail prices).

highlights.title: Whispering Complaints Into Your Phone May Be the Future of Customer Feedback
highlights.summary: Forget email surveys or long calls spent on hold. Voicebox lets people send customer feedback by recording a voice note on their phone.
body: Some of the hottest software this year revolves around capturing voices. Whether it’s the sharp dictations of Wispr or the always-listening ears of Granola, voice-centered software currently feels inescapable. Voice dictation is getting so sharp, in fact, that I often write drafts in my notepad and then dictate aloud to my laptop.

Some prognosticators have declared this to be a dramatic end-of-the-keyboard moment, where legions of white-collar workers will soon be quietly whispering into desk microphones rather than clacking away at keyboards. I disagree, but I do think these changes could upend how customers give feedback.

I rarely email customer support unless something substantially negative has happened and I’m fishing for a refund. I’m much more open to giving feedback by blabbering for 20 seconds into my phone, good or bad, than I am to waiting on hold for who knows how long until someone answers.

highlights.title: Pokémon TCG Destined Rivals ETB in Stock at Amazon and Under Market Price
highlights.summary: Amazon has restocked the rare Pokémon TCG Destined Rivals Elite Trainer Box for under market price.
body: As I've mentioned in a few different articles today, Amazon has been restocking a whole bunch of rare Pokémon TCG sets for Labor Day, and there are some seriously sought-after sets up for grabs right now. That includes the rare Destined Rivals Elite Trainer Box, which is currently available for just under $116 from Amazon.

I can't remember the last time one of these bad boys was available anywhere near market price from a major retailer. Yes, it's still well above the original MSRP, but that's unfortunately the state of the Pokémon TCG market right now. If you're willing to pay the premium, Amazon is currently one of the better places to pick one up.

TCGplayer has a median listing price of around $150, while its current market price sits at $120.18. Once you factor in delivery costs as well, Amazon's $115.98 price starts to look pretty reasonable, particularly given that it's sold and shipped directly by Amazon.
If you've been waiting for a restock, this is probably one worth considering while the stock lasts. These don't tend to hang around for long when they appear at major retailers.

highlights.summary: On Sunday, the Israeli-American Council launched a petition, calling for the rapper's removal from the remaining tour dates of Ed Sheeran's Loop Tour.
body: Macklemore is doubling down after facing backlash from a pro- Israel organization over his “Free Palestine ” public plea while opening for Ed Sheeran ‘s Loop Tour.

On Monday, the rapper wrote on social media, “Wanting all humans to be treated equal should never be controversial.” His post also included his speech from Saturday, the second night of back-to-back shows at New Jersey’s MetLife Stadium.

“So I say Free Palestine, I say Free Lebanon, I say Free Cuba, I say Free Congo, Free Sudan, I say Free all people in America living in fear of this terrorist organization, ICE. None of us will be free until we are all free,” he added.

This came a day after Macklemore’s opening set on Friday drew criticism for the rapper’s performance of his protest song “Hind’s Hall” and telling the audience, “A big part of the reason why I wanted to do this tour in the first place is so I could stand up in stadiums like this and say two words that are very near and dear to my heart: Free Palestine.”

highlights.title: A health MOT is just one step towards prevention | Letters
highlights.summary: Tackling social and economic conditions must come first, writes Dr Louise Lawson. Plus letters from James Hibberd, Bob Forster and Dr Giles Youngs. Devi Sridhar is right to welcome free cholesterol testing on the NHS in England and blood pressure checks in pharmacies.
body: Sridhar’s proposed five-point health MOT is undoubtedly valuable, but it is better understood as identifying risk rather than preventing disease. Prevention is what comes next: enabling people to make changes that improve health and reduce that risk. Public health has long distinguished between upstream factors, such as poverty, housing, employment, access to affordable healthy food and safe green spaces, and downstream interventions focused on individuals. Screening and health checks sit much closer to the downstream end of that spectrum.

Interventions aimed at changing behaviour emphasise individual responsibility and often assume that everyone has similar economic, social and psychological resources to adopt healthier lifestyles. Yet those living on low incomes, in insecure work or facing linguistic and cultural barriers often have far less capacity to act on health advice. Such approaches can also reinforce stigma by implying that poor health results primarily from individual choices rather than the circumstances in which people live, while diverting attention from the drivers of health inequalities.
points: Tackling social and economic conditions must come first, writes Dr Louise Lawson.
Plus letters from James Hibberd, Bob Forster and Dr Giles Youngs.

Prevention is what comes next: enabling people to make changes that improve health and reduce that risk.

highlights.summary: Oliver Lines seals a shock 4-2 win over world number one Zhao Xintong in the first round of the English Open.
body: Oliver Lines stunned Zhao Xintong with a 4-2 win over the world number one in the first round of the English Open.
China's Zhao, the 2025 world champion, made two century breaks as the tie was level at 2-2 following the first four frames.
But England's Lines, 31, compiled breaks of 77 and 84 to win the next two frames and set up a last-32 meeting with Yuan Sijun in Brentwood.
"You try not to think about it, but you know if you don't play somewhere near your best then you are going home."

highlights.title: Next Hunger Games Movie 'Sunrise' Confirms Switching Genres in 'Return to Form'
highlights.summary: Francis Lawrence has been making Hunger Games movies long enough to bring the series back to a “return to form.” He joined the franchise with Catching Fire in 2013, and now, five films later, November’s Sunrise on the Reaping finds him staging another Quarter Quell in another spectacular arena…
body: But as much as Sunrise goes back to basics, Lawrence and longtime series producer Nina Jacobson were just as excited to finally tell Haymitch’s story, an arc that takes him from an “optimistic kind of carefree kid” to the bitter alcoholic Katniss meets in the first movie. Ultimately, it’s the story of an apolitical young man radicalized into defender of District 12 and beyond. Lawrence sees the film as particularly relevant to the moment.
“When something’s wrong, you have to stand up,” he said. “You have to say something. You have to fight.”

That idea — of Sunrise as both an echo of Catching Fire and the hidden beginning of the revolution Katniss would one day lead — loomed over the gut-wrenching preview footage. So when I had the chance to sit down with Lawrence and Jacobson afterward for an exclusive interview, I jumped at the chance to dig further into how they built that connection.
Francis, you emphasize that Sunrise on the Reaping feels like a return in some ways. What does that mean? Why did The Hunger Games need a return?

highlights.title: French President Emmanuel Macron Calls on YouTube to Finance Content and Warns of Growing Threat to Cultural Model (EXCLUSIVE)
highlights.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron said the Lumière Summit in Saint-Paul-de-Vence, which he co-chaired with South Korean President Lee Jae Myung on Monday, was deliberately held at a moment of dramatic upheaval for the entertainment business, from the growing dominance of YouTube and TikTok to AI and…
body: Macron said the Lumière Summit in Saint-Paul-de-Vence was deliberately being held at a moment of dramatic upheaval for the entertainment business, from the growing dominance of YouTube and TikTok to AI.

He argued that YouTube, which is currently outtalking Netflix in over 20 international markets, should increasingly be brought into the same ecosystem as other global platforms such as Netflix, Amazon and Disney, that have been required to invest in local production.

France and other countries need to “engage with them” in a multilateral way, he said, to try to change the platform’s approach so that it helps finance “local content,” while supporting “more creativity, more creations, more respect of the authors.”

Macron, who’s been a driving force behind the rise of French AI companies, including Mistral, as well as the creation of the EU’s AI Act and the international summit on AI that was held last year, also said France wanted to compete aggressively in AI by expanding computing capacity, data centers and European models. But he insisted that technological ambition must be accompanied by protections for intellectual property and much greater transparency.

highlights.title: The Best Kitchen Composter Actually Makes Compost With No Stench or Mess
highlights.summary: Electric composting machines and food recyclers promise to turn food scraps into grounds with zero stench and minimal cleanup. Here are the ones we recommend.
body: I consider myself a fairly eco-conscious person. I reduce, reuse, recycle; I take public transit; I avoid using AI for meme-making and learning celebrity heights. But composting never really took. I'd try to gather food scraps in a plastic countertop compost bin in my kitchen, but emptying and cleaning the receptacle every couple days was messy and smelly and I'd give up after a couple weeks. In 2025, however, New York City made composting the law of the land and I knew I needed to figure out a more sustainable solution.

Electric kitchen composters and food recyclers promise to turn your food scraps into dried grounds or usable compost in a matter of hours, eliminating the need to transport a dripping bag of rotting food goo through your apartment and around the block to where your building keeps the communal bin (just me?). Like magic, these machines can reduce the volume of your food waste by up to 90%, so you can go weeks or months without emptying them. The downside? Many of them are very expensive.

highlights.title: Fortnite Officially Bringing Mega Man to the Island with Tournament and Skins
highlights.summary: Mega Man is still one of the most anticipated Fortnite collaborations coming in Chapter 7 Season 4. It has been teased since the previous season ended, and despite Mega Man items being in the battle royale games, fans are patiently waiting for the skins to be added to Fortnite.
body: Fortnite Override, also known as Chapter 7 Season 4, focuses on two themes: retro games and hacking. This has allowed Epic Games to introduce an array of beloved video game characters to Fortnite. Mega Man was one of the first characters to be teased for this season, as a Mega Man cartridge was inserted into the override console that spawned after the Unstable Event at the Zero Point. However, over two weeks into the season, he has yet to make an appearance.

This is about to change, as a Mega Man Cup will be held on Tuesday, Sept. 8, giving players the opportunity to obtain Mega Man cosmetics for free before they hit the Item Shop. The rules have not been revealed yet, but according to leakers, it is a duos tournament set in Battle Royale, Zero Build, and mobile servers.

Comparing the Mega Man Cup's promotional image to previous Mega Man footage shown in the trailer, it's likely that fans will receive the standard skin as well as the Mega Man X alternative style. Since skins tend to hit the Item Shop not long after they are given away in cups, players can expect Mega Man to become available on Wednesday or Thursday.

It has been teased since the previous season ended, and despite Mega Man items being in the battle royale games, fans are patiently waiting for the skins to be added to Fortnite.

highlights.title: My favorite family heirloom: an old Zojirushi hot water dispenser better than any tea kettle
highlights.summary: It heats water up fast and crucially, keeps it warm for the whole day, so you can can access hot water to your heart’s content. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: O f all the things my mother has given me from the vast warehouse of her garage, there are two items I treasure the most. One, a Costco-sized box of gallon-sized Ziploc bags, and two, a battered Zojirushi water boiler that has been in the family for decades. The Ziploc bags are nice to have and can be easily replaced; the water boiler, on the other hand, has become an indispensable tool that makes my life at home a little better, every time I use it.

A brief twist: if given the choice, I’d take an ice cold beverage over hot any time. But even I, with my preference for drinks so cold that they hurt my teeth, have been converted to my family’s beloved Zojirushi.

I use it almost every day – for the instant Cafe Bustelo coffee that I drink every morning, for instant noodles, for tea and hot chocolate and any other wintry weather beverage. Once you’ve opened your heart (and wallet) to one of these things, I promise you that you will never look back.

highlights.title: Audi’s new A2 E-tron is its most affordable and efficient EV yet
highlights.summary: When shopping for an electric vehicle, affordability is becoming a more common trait. But affordable and energy efficient is truly a rare breed. Often you have to sacrifice one for the other. Want something affordable? Great, here's a range loser. Want something that goes the distance?
body: Unfortunately it won’t be making it’s way to North America any time soon.

Surprisingly, here comes Audi to split the difference. The German automaker’s new A2 E-tron compact crossover is inexpensive, starting at just £32,200 (about $45,000). And it absolutely impresses with an ultra low drag coefficient and a range of battery and drivetrain options that, when configured correctly, can produce a range of up to 401 miles.

Unfortunately for us Yanks, this rear-wheel drive compact car is just for the European market for now. But perhaps Audi will eventually see the error of its ways, or Americans will get their heads out of their tailpipes long enough to see the real advantages of a highly efficient, compact EV with an Audi badge.

Efficient is often synonymous with aerodynamic, and the A2 E-tron certainly confirms that. Flush door handles, cool air intakes, a fully enclosed underbody, and gap reducers around the wheel arches help reduce the drag coefficient down to 0.24, a first for Audi. Another first is bidirectional charging, which will help support vehicle-t0-load via an outlet in the trunk, or vehicle-to-home with the right compatible DC wall box.
points: When shopping for an electric vehicle, affordability is becoming a more common trait.
But affordable and energy efficient is truly a rare breed.

highlights.title: Maresca eyes rest for busy dad Haaland as Manchester City prepare for Porto
highlights.summary: Norwegian forward has played every minute of season. Parenting duties have changed player’s ‘priorities’ Enzo Maresca believes Erling Haaland has become “complete” as his priorities have changed after the birth of the Manchester City No 9’s son two years ago.
body: Haaland has again started the campaign in prolific form, scoring three goals in City’s opening three Premier League victories. In three of the 26‑year‑old’s four previous seasons at City he has won the Premier League golden boot. Maresca pointed to how the birth of his son in 2024 changed the Norwegian’s motivation.

The manager said: “He’s a man now. He’s a dad. When he arrived here [in summer 2022] he was not a dad and now he’s a dad and life completely changes because the priority becomes his son. I’m happy for him because he was already top as a player and as a boy but now you can see that he is complete. He is a family man, he is still scoring goals so I’m very happy for him.”

City are at Porto in the opening league‑phase game of the Champions League on Tuesday. Haaland has played every competitive minute of the campaign so far, and Maresca said he will be rested at some point, particularly as as the striker was part of the Norway team that reached the World Cup quarter-finals.

highlights.title: The Legend of Zelda's Best Amiibo Finally Arrives This Month
highlights.summary: Back in May, to mark the third anniversary of the release of The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom, Nintendo unveiled a new amiibo figure tied to the game, due this month. It might be the best Tears of the Kingdom figurine yet.
body: Nintendo's new Mineru's Construct amiibo will be available starting Sept. 17. It's a relatively large-scale figure representing the ancient Zonai robot originally used by the Sage of Spirit, Mineru, and rebuilt and commanded by Link toward the end of the game's storyline.
Best of all, it has fully articulated, posable arms! "There's a fair bit of freedom to its movement too, so try making it pose in a way that looks good to you," recommends Nintendo, helpfully.

As with other amiibo, tapping the Mineru's Construct on your Switch's NFC reader will reward you with helpful items in-game. Notably, there's a chance to get a special fabric for Link's paraglider with a Mineru's Construct theme and glow-in-the-dark elements.

It's anyone's guess why Nintendo is choosing to release the Mineru's Construct amiibo almost three years after the game (and a year after its Switch 2 edition of Tears of the Kingdom ). Although it's worth noting that the very existence of the Construct could be considered a late-game spoiler for Tears of the Kingdom.

highlights.title: How To Reset The Camera Settings On Your iPhone
highlights.summary: We all want to take the best photos with our $1,000 devices, and sometimes that means rolling back all those extra settings in the Camera app back to zero.
body: Changing your iPhone camera settings back to default is pretty simple, so long as you don’t mind flipping a few dozen toggles.

While it's unlikely your iPhone will ever beat out a purpose-built camera, there's a lot you can do to optimize its capture quality. Even an out-of-date iPhone will be chock-a-block with ways to take your photography and videography to the next level. However, sometimes the best way to measure that improvement is by going back to the basics of default settings.

There are many ways to improve your smartphone photography with any model, and iPhones are no different; there are thousands of great guides to help you choose the right settings for the pictures and videos you want. On the other hand, it can be hard to judge the change in quality if you've already spent a long time messing with your settings — or if you have a second-hand phone that arrived pre-muddled. Sometimes, it's desirable to bring your camera back to default settings and build from there, but there's no single button to carry out that reset. Luckily, it's still relatively simple to set everything back to default.

body: “Obviously everybody’s responsible, including me, for doing things properly,” Belichick said. “And we intend to do that.”

The Tar Heels were off following their season-opening win against TCU in Ireland on 29 August. But during that open week, general manager Michael Lombardi resigned after being put on paid administrative leave in late July amid the university’s investigation into his conduct.

The same day, Raleigh TV station WRAL cited anonymous sources in reporting the type of questions asked of some interviewees. Some focused on Belichick’s son Steve, the Tar Heels’ defensive coordinator, who is currently on medical leave. There have also been allegations that Steve Belichick has been questioned by lawyers over issues related to drug use.

Additionally, Lombardi attorney Tom Mars told The Athletic that the school’s investigation now included questions into potential “inappropriate” relationships that didn’t involve his client. Two people with knowledge of the situation had previously told the AP that a human resources complaint from a former employee was tied to Lombardi originally being placed on leave as the investigation launched.

highlights.title: NHL 27 Is Using AI-Generated Voiceover for In-Game Commentators, John Buccigross Says
highlights.summary: EA Sports is using generative AI to create voiceover for its in-game commentators in NHL 27, according to veteran sports commentator John Buccigross. When speaking on the Chirping Zebras podcast (initially spotted by Insider Gaming's Mike Straw ), Buccigross was talking about his experience working…
body: "They're using some AI now; they played me some stuff back of my voice," said Buccigross. "It's like 'Wow, that's pretty good!' If that means less work but the same check, I'll take it. Sometimes AI will get something wrong. One of the guys was playing it back, and a lot of these guys maybe aren't hardcore sports fans; they're video game extrordinares. They're not always up on the vernacular. So they're playing back my AI voice, and they're like, 'Score! And the crowd gets out of their chairs!' I was like, 'No, they're not chairs. They look like chairs, but we call them seats.'

"So, little things like that, you gotta go back and listen because words matter. But then you can make AI smarter; in the future they'll say seats, they won't say chairs. You have to manually put that in. That was kind of a funny anecdote from the process."
